title: Mounting Headwinds For US Assets
gist: Teaser only: Louis-Vincent Gave restates Gavekal's thesis that US outperformance is ending after a 2024 post-election blow-off top, and asks whether recent events revive or stall it. The body is paywalled and truncated.

insights.claim: Gavekal's running research theme for the past few years is that the age of massive US outperformance is drawing to an end.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Frames a structural case for diversifying away from US assets.
insights.quote: the age of massive US outperformance was drawing to an end
insights.locator: The point of the Daily reports

insights.claim: The surge in US relative performance that accompanied Donald Trump's 2024 election victory was probably an exponential blow-off top, typical of climactic bull markets.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: If a blow-off top, US relative performance may mean-revert sharply.
insights.quote: an exponential “blow-off top” that is fairly typical of climactic bull markets

insights.claim: The open question as of 9 Nov 2026 is whether recent events revive US outperformance or stall it; the full answer is paywalled, but the title points to mounting headwinds for US assets.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Watch for events that confirm or negate the end-of-US-outperformance narrative.
insights.quote: whether recent events will revive US outperformance? Or stall it?
